sections.h2: Where does a Miami County deed get recorded?
sections.html:
Deeds for Miami County property are recorded at the Recorder's Office, 201 West Main Street, Troy, OH 45373. The office answers at (937) 440-6040, takes faxes at (937) 440-6034, and keeps counter hours of 8 am to 4 pm, Monday through Friday, per its county page.

The Recorder keeps the permanent chain of title: deeds, mortgages, easements, leases, plats and veteran discharges. Valuation and the tax bill sit with other offices. The county's Recorder Resources page says the Auditor sets values and assessments and the Treasurer collects taxes, while the Clerk of Courts handles property disputes. In a typical year the office handles 15,169 documents, among them 6,259 deeds and 4,319 mortgages, and 9,806 of the total arrive electronically.

sections.h2: What does the Miami County Recorder charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
The first two pages cost $39.00 and every added page costs $8.00, according to the office's documents and fees page. That price already folds in a $5.00 preservation fee, and part of each fee is passed to the state for the Ohio Housing Trust Fund under sections 317.32 and 317.36.

Miami County sample recording fees, effective January 1, 2025, from the Recorder's fee page
Document lengthRecording fee
1 or 2 pages$39.00
3 pages$47.00
4 pages$55.00
6 pages$71.00
10 pages$103.00

Other charges that can land on a sale or a payoff:

  • A $4.00 marginal notation fee for a mortgage release, assignment or modification.
  • A $20.00 fee when a document breaks the Ohio standardization guidelines.
  • No fee to record or copy a military discharge (DD-214).

Mail the original with a self-addressed stamped envelope so it comes back to you.

sections.h2: What approvals come before the Recorder in Miami County?
sections.html:
A deed must clear the County Engineer and the Auditor first. Miami County's conveyance standards, adopted August 12, 2025, say every instrument is approved for transfer by the Engineer's Office, with a signed DTE 100 value statement or a DTE 100EX exemption form turned in alongside it.

Three rules in those standards matter to sellers:

  • No transfer is approved when the grantor never appears as an earlier grantee, unless the deed or an affidavit under section 5301.252 explains the gap in the chain of title.
  • A deed that carves a piece off an existing parcel, or changes the legal description, needs a boundary survey plat that the Engineer reviews.
  • Anyone claiming an exemption must prove it to the Auditor. If doubt remains, the fee is charged or the parcel does not transfer.

The conveyance fee itself comes from section 319.54: $1, or ten cents for each $100 of value, whichever is more. A county may add a transfer tax of up to thirty cents per $100 under section 322.02. The grantor pays both, so ask the Miami County Auditor which ones apply before you fill out your closing statement.

sections.h2: What does the Miami County value statement ask the seller?
sections.html:
Under section 319.202, the buyer's statement records whether the seller expects a reduced tax bill, such as the homestead or owner-occupancy credit, and whether the land was enrolled in the agricultural use valuation. A yes on either needs a sworn paper that both sides have accounted for the amount.

Farm ground is worth a question in a county that covers 410 square miles and has only five cities. If a seller's acreage was enrolled, leaving the program can trigger a recoupment charge, and the statute wants it priced into the deal before the deed goes to the Auditor.

When the house is a rental, the Auditor stamps the deed with a reminder that the buyer must file landlord information under section 5323.02.

sections.h2: How can you look up or copy Miami County land records?
sections.html:
The county's records search page offers a free basic search by last and first name, or business name, in the AVA database. Images carry a watermark, and a watermarked copy is not accepted for recording.

  • Basic search: free to view and print, with a watermark.
  • Clean copies: email or call the Recorder's Office; since January 2026 copies cost $2.00 per page, paid in advance.
  • Credit cards: a service fee of $2.00 or 2.65% applies, whichever is greater. Cash and check are also taken.
  • Title searchers: Laredo Anywhere, run by Fidlar Technology, reaches deeds back to the county's start in 1807.

Deeds from 1807 through 1979 are scanned as whole books. Records for 1980 through 2008 are only partly indexed, and for anything before 1980 the county asks you to contact the office. Certified copies run $2.00 per page plus $1.00 for each seal.

sections.h2: Can a title company e-record a Miami County deed?
sections.html:
E-recording exists, but the county describes it as a tool for businesses that file regularly, not for one-time submissions. Its e-recording page lists five vendors: ePN, Simplifile, Hopdox, Indecomm and CSC. Each sets its own pricing, so a title agent signs up with a vendor directly.

A private seller closing without a title company can mail the deed or bring it to the counter. Ask the Recorder's Office at (937) 440-6040 whether your document type can go electronically before you plan around it.

sections.h2: What is Miami County like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Miami County was founded March 1, 1807, takes its name from the Miami people, and has Troy as its seat. Per Wikipedia, it covers 410 square miles in the Dayton metro area and borders Shelby, Champaign, Clark, Montgomery and Darke counties. The cities are Troy, Piqua and Tipp City, with parts of Huber Heights and Union.

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts shows a 2025 population estimate of 112,634, up 3.5% since 2020, and 47,930 housing units. About 73.4% of homes are owner-occupied, the median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 is $229,100, and median household income is $76,817. Commuters average 22.0 minutes to work, and the county issued 340 building permits in 2025.

Whatever the condition of the house or who lives in it, every sale ends with the same steps above: Engineer, Auditor, then Recorder.

faqs.q: Where is the Miami County Recorder's Office?
faqs.a: It is at 201 West Main Street in Troy, OH 45373. The phone is (937) 440-6040 and hours are 8 am to 4 pm, Monday through Friday.

faqs.q: How much is it to record a deed in Miami County?
faqs.a: The county charges $39.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each page after that, including a $5.00 preservation fee. A $4.00 marginal notation fee applies to mortgage releases, assignments and modifications, and a $20.00 fee applies when a document misses the Ohio standardization rules.

faqs.q: Who pays the conveyance fee on a Miami County sale?
faqs.a: The grantor, meaning the seller, pays it to the Auditor before the deed goes to the Recorder. The statute sets $1 or ten cents per $100, whichever is greater, and any county transfer tax is added on top. Ask the Auditor what applies to your parcel.

faqs.q: Does Miami County need a survey to split a parcel?
faqs.a: Yes. The county's conveyance standards require a boundary survey plat when a deed cuts up an existing parcel or changes its legal description, and the County Engineer reviews it before the Auditor accepts the deed.

faqs.q: Can I print my deed for free in Miami County?
faqs.a: Yes, the basic records search lets you view and print a watermarked copy at no charge. A copy without the watermark must be requested from the Recorder's Office and costs $2.00 per page.
